    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Forward
Looking Statements</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">This

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Financial Corp., MHC</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Financial Corp., MHC is a federally chartered mutual holding company and
currently owns 74.4% of the outstanding shares of common stock of Oritani
Financial Corp.&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp., MHC has not engaged in any
significant business activity other than owning the common stock of Oritani
Financial Corp., and does not intend to expand its business
activities.&#160;&#160;So long as Oritani Financial Corp., MHC exists, it is
required to own a majority of the voting stock of Oritani Financial
Corp.&#160;&#160;The executive office of Oritani Financial Corp., MHC, is
located at 370 Pascack Road, in the Township of Washington, New Jersey 07676,
and its telephone number is (201) 664-5400.&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp.,
MHC is subject to comprehensive regulation and examination by the Office of
Thrift Supervision (&#8220;OTS&#8221;).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Financial Corp.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Financial Corp. is the federally chartered mid-tier stock holding company of
Oritani Bank.&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp. owns 100% of the outstanding
shares of common stock of Oritani Bank.&#160;&#160;Since being formed in 1998,
Oritani Financial Corp. has engaged primarily in the business of holding the
common stock of Oritani Bank as well as two limited liability companies that own
a variety of real estate investments.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Oritani Financial
Corp.&#8217;s executive office is located at 370 Pascack Road, in the Township of
Washington, New Jersey 07676, and its telephone number is (201)
664-5400.&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp. is subject to comprehensive
regulation and examination by the OTS.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, Oritani
Financial Corp. had consolidated assets of $1.91 billion, consolidated deposits
of $1.13 billion and consolidated stockholders&#8217; equity of $240.1
million.&#160;&#160;Its consolidated net income for the fiscal year ended June
30, 2009 was $5.6 million.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Bank</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">General</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Bank is a New Jersey-chartered savings bank headquartered in the Township of
Washington, New Jersey.&#160;&#160;Oritani Bank was originally founded in 1911,
as a New Jersey building and loan association.&#160;&#160;Over the years,
Oritani Bank has expanded through internal growth as well as through a series of
business combinations.&#160;&#160;In 1997, Oritani Bank converted to a mutual
savings bank charter, and in March 1998, reorganized into the two-tier mutual
holding company structure.&#160;&#160;Oritani Bank conducts business from its
main office located at 370 Pascack Road, in the Township of Washington, New
Jersey 07676, and its 20 branch offices located in the New Jersey Counties of
Bergen, Hudson and Passaic.&#160;&#160;The telephone number at its main office
is (201) 664-5400.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our assets totaled $1.91 billion
and our deposits totaled $1.13 billion.&#160;&#160;Oritani Bank was formerly
known as Oritani Savings Bank.&#160;&#160;Effective September 8, 2008, the name
was changed to Oritani Bank.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
principal business consists of attracting retail and commercial bank deposits
from the general public in the areas surrounding our main office in the Township
of Washington, New Jersey and our branch offices located in the New Jersey
Counties of Bergen (15 branches, including our main office), Hudson (5 branches)
and Passaic (one branch), and investing those deposits, together with funds
generated from operations, in multi-family and commercial real estate loans,
one- to four-family residential mortgage loans as well as in second mortgage and
equity loans, construction loans, business loans, other consumer loans, and
investment securities.&#160;&#160;We originate loans primarily for investment
and hold such loans in our portfolio.&#160;&#160;Occasionally, we will also
enter into loan participations.&#160;&#160;Our revenues are derived principally
from interest on loans and securities as well as our investments in real estate
and real estate joint ventures.&#160;&#160;We also generate revenues from fees
and service charges and other income.&#160;&#160;Our primary sources of funds
are deposits, borrowings and principal and interest payments on loans and
securities.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Oritani
Financial Corp. completed its initial public stock offering on January 23,
2007.&#160;&#160;The Company sold 12,165,649 shares, or 30.0% of its outstanding
common stock, to subscribers in the offering, including 1,589,644 shares
purchased by the Oritani Bank Employee Stock Ownership Plan
(&#8220;ESOP&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp., MHC, the Company&#8217;s federally
chartered mutual holding company parent, holds 27,575,476 shares, which
represented 68.0% of the Company&#8217;s outstanding common stock at the conclusion of
the initial public offering.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Bank contributed $1.0
million in cash, and the Company issued 811,037 shares of common stock, or 2.0%
of the Company&#8217;s outstanding common stock, to the OritaniBank Charitable
Foundation.&#160;&#160;Proceeds from the offering, including the value of shares
issued to the charitable foundation but net of expenses, were $127.6
million.&#160;&#160;Net deployable funds, after deducting for the ESOP shares
and the total contribution to the charitable foundation, were $102.6
million.&#160;&#160;The Company contributed $59.7 million of the proceeds to
Oritani Bank.&#160;&#160;Stock oversubscription proceeds of $323.4 million were
returned to subscribers. So long as Oritani Financial Corp., MHC exists, it is
required to own a majority of the voting stock of Oritani Financial
Corp.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
website address is <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.oritani.com</font>.&#160;&#160;Information
on our website should not be considered a part of this report.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Market
Area</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">From our
headquarters in the Township of Washington, New Jersey, we operate twenty one
full service branches, including our main office.&#160;&#160;We operate branches
in three separate counties of New Jersey:&#160;&#160;Bergen, Hudson and
Passaic.&#160;&#160;The majority of our branches, fifteen, and deposits are
located in Bergen County.&#160;&#160;In addition, we operate five branches in
Hudson County and one branch in Passaic County.&#160;&#160;We are in the process
of opening an additional branch in Bergen County.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In terms
of population rank, Bergen County ranks as the largest county in New Jersey
while Hudson County ranks fifth and Passaic County ranks ninth out of twenty-one
counties.&#160;&#160;Based upon household income statistics, Bergen County
ranks&#160;fourth out of the twenty-one counties in New Jersey while Passaic
ranks&#160;seventeenth and Hudson County ranks twentieth.&#160;&#160;The three
counties are a part of New Jersey, which is referred to as the &#8220;Gateway
Region.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The economy in our primary market area has benefited from
being varied and diverse. It is largely urban and suburban with a broad economic
base as is typical for counties surrounding the New York metropolitan
area.&#160;&#160;As one of the wealthiest states in the nation, New Jersey, with
a population of 8.7 million, is considered one of the most attractive banking
markets in the United States. The June 2009 unemployment rate for New Jersey of
9.2% was slightly lower than the national rate of 9.5%.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Item 1A,
Risk Factors &#8211; Current Market and Economic Conditions May Significantly Affect
Our Operations and Financial Condition.&#8221;</font></div><br>

        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Bergen
County is bordered by Rockland County, New York to the north, the Hudson River
to the east, Hudson County to the south, a small border with Essex County also
to the south and Passaic County to the west.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Hudson
County has always been a gateway for many immigrants to the United
States.&#160;&#160;It is also recognized as one of the Northeast&#8217;s major
transportation and industrial hubs as the New York metropolitan area&#8217;s three
major airports &#8211; John F. Kennedy International Airport, LaGuardia Airport, and
Newark Liberty International Airport &#8211; are within a relatively short distance of
Hudson County.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Passaic
County is bordered by Orange County, New York to the north, Rockland County, New
York to the northeast, Bergen County to the east, Essex County to the south,
Morris County to the southwest and Sussex County to the west.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Competition</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We face
intense competition within our market area both in making loans and attracting
deposits.&#160;&#160;Our market area has a high concentration of financial
institutions including large money center and regional banks, community banks
and credit unions.&#160;&#160;Some of our competitors offer products and
services that we currently do not offer, such as trust services and private
banking.&#160;&#160;As of June 30, 2008, the latest date for which statistics
are available, our market share of deposits was approximately 1.8% in Bergen
County, and less than 1.0% in each of Hudson and Passaic Counties.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
competition for loans and deposits comes principally from locally owned and
out-of-state commercial banks, savings institutions, mortgage banking firms,
insurance companies and credit unions.&#160;&#160;We face additional competition
for deposits from short-term money market funds, brokerage firms, mutual funds
and insurance companies.&#160;&#160;Our primary focus is to build and develop
profitable customer relationships across all lines of business while maintaining
our role as a community bank.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Lending
Activities</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
principal lending activity is the origination of multi-family loans and
commercial real estate loans as well as residential real estate mortgage loans
and construction loans secured by property located primarily in our market
area.&#160;&#160;Our multi-family loans consist primarily of mortgage loans
secured by apartment buildings.&#160;&#160;Our commercial real estate loans
consist primarily of mortgage loans secured by commercial offices, retail space,
warehouses and mixed-use buildings.&#160;&#160;Our residential real estate
mortgage loans consist of one- to four-family residential real property and
consumer loans.&#160;&#160;Construction loans consist primarily of one- to
four-family development, condominiums and commercial development
projects.&#160;&#160;We curtailed construction lending in 2009 due to current
market and economic conditions and expect to maintain this posture for the
foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;Second mortgage and equity loans consist
primarily of home equity loans and home equity lines of
credit.&#160;&#160;Multi-family and commercial real estate loans represented
$839.7 million, or 64.5%, of our total loan portfolio at June 30, 2009. One- to
four-family residential real estate mortgage loans represented $266.0 million,
or 20.4%, of our total loan portfolio at June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;We also offer
second mortgages and equity loans.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, such loans
totaled $54.8 million, or 4.2%, of our loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;At June 30,
2009, construction and land loans totaled $130.8 million, or 10.0%, of our loan
portfolio.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, other loans, which primarily consist of
business and to a smaller extent, account loans, totaled $11.0 million, or less
than 1.0%, of our loan portfolio.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">First
Mortgage Loans:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Conventional One-
to Four-Family Residential Loans.</font>&#160;&#160;We originate one- to
four-family residential mortgage loans substantially all of which are secured by
properties located in our primary market area.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009,
$266.0 million, or 20.4% of our loan portfolio, consisted of one- to four-family
residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;We generally retain for our portfolio
substantially all of these loans that we originate.&#160;&#160;One- to
four-family mortgage loan originations are generally obtained from existing or
past customers, through advertising, and through referrals from local builders,
real estate brokers, and attorneys and are underwritten pursuant to Oritani
Bank&#8217;s policies and standards.&#160;&#160;In 2008, the Company began a program
where a fee is paid to a broker for a loan referral that results in an
origination or a purchase of a recently closed loan.&#160;&#160;Generally, one-
to four-family residential mortgage loans are originated in amounts up to 80% of
the lesser of the appraised value or purchase price of the property, with
private mortgage insurance required on loans with a loan-to-value ratio in
excess of 80%.&#160;&#160;We generally will not make loans with a loan-to-value
ratio in excess of 90%.&#160;&#160;Fixed rate mortgage loans are originated for
terms of up to 40 years.&#160;&#160;Generally, fixed rate residential mortgage
loans are underwritten according to Freddie Mac guidelines, policies and
procedures, with a maximum origination amount of $2.0 million.&#160;&#160;We do
not originate or purchase, and our loan portfolio does not include, any
sub-prime loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also
offer adjustable rate mortgage loans for one- to four-family properties, with an
interest rate based on the weekly average yield on U.S. Treasuries adjusted to a
constant maturity of one-year, which adjust either annually or every three years
from the outset of the loan or which adjusts annually after a five-, seven- or
ten-year initial fixed rate period.&#160;&#160;Originations and purchases of
adjustable rate one- to four-family residential loans totaled $27.7 million
during the fiscal year ended June 30, 2009 as compared to total originations and
purchases of $89.9 million of one- to four-family residential loans during the
same fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Our adjustable rate mortgage loans generally
provide for maximum rate adjustments of 2% per adjustment, with a lifetime
maximum adjustment up to 6%, regardless of the initial rate.&#160;&#160;Our
adjustable rate mortgage loans amortize over terms of up to 30
years.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Adjustable
rate mortgage loans decrease the risk associated with changes in market interest
rates by periodically repricing, but involve other risks because, as interest
rates increase, the underlying payments by the borrower increase, thus
increasing the potential for default by the borrower.&#160;&#160;At the same
time, the marketability of the underlying collateral may be adversely affected
by higher interest rates.&#160;&#160;Upward adjustment of the contractual
interest rate is also limited by the maximum periodic and lifetime interest rate
adjustments permitted by our loan documents and, therefore, the effectiveness of
adjustable rate mortgage loans may be limited during periods of rapidly rising
interest rates.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009 $46.2 million, or 17.4% of our one-
to four-family residential real estate loans, had adjustable rates of
interest.</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In an
effort to provide financing for first-time homebuyers, we offer our own
first-time homebuyer loan program.&#160;&#160;This program offers one- to
four-family residential mortgage loans to qualified
individuals.&#160;&#160;These loans are offered with terms and adjustable and
fixed rates of interest similar to our other one- to four-family mortgage loan
products.&#160;&#160;With this program, borrowers receive a discounted mortgage
interest rate and do not pay certain loan origination fees.&#160;&#160;Such
loans must be secured by an owner-occupied residence.&#160;&#160;These loans are
originated using similar underwriting guidelines as our other one- to
four-family mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Such loans are originated in amounts of
up to 90% of the lower of the property&#8217;s appraised value or the sale
price.&#160;&#160;Private mortgage insurance is not required for such
loans.&#160;&#160;The maximum amount of such loan is $275,000.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also
offer our directors, officers and employees who satisfy certain criteria and our
general underwriting standards fixed or adjustable rate loan products with
reduced interest rates.&#160;&#160;Employee loans adhere to all other terms and
conditions contained in the loan policy.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">All
residential mortgage loans that we originate include &#8220;due-on-sale&#8221; clauses,
which give us the right to declare a loan immediately due and payable in the
event that, among other things, the borrower sells or otherwise disposes of the
real property subject to the mortgage and the loan is not
repaid.&#160;&#160;Regulations limit the amount that a savings bank may lend
relative to the appraised value of the real estate securing the loan, as
determined by an appraisal of the property at the time the loan is
originated.&#160;&#160;All borrowers are required to obtain title insurance for
the benefit of Oritani Bank.&#160;&#160;We also require homeowner&#8217;s insurance
and fire and casualty insurance and, where circumstances warrant, flood
insurance on properties securing real estate loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Multi-Family and
Commercial Real Estate Loans.&#160;&#160;</font>We originate non-residential
commercial real estate mortgage loans and loans on multi-family
dwellings.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, $839.7 million, or 64.6% of our loan
portfolio, consisted of multi-family and commercial real estate
loans.&#160;&#160;Our commercial real estate mortgage loans are primarily
permanent loans secured by improved property such as mixed-use properties,
office buildings, retail stores and commercial warehouses.&#160;&#160;Our
multi-family mortgage loans are primarily permanent loans secured by apartment
buildings.&#160;&#160;The typical loan has a fixed rate of interest for the
first five years, after which the loan reprices to a market index plus a
spread.&#160;&#160;The fixed rate period is occasionally extended to as much as
ten years.&#160;&#160;These loans typically amortize over 25 years and the
maximum amortization period is 30 years.&#160;&#160;We also offer such loans on
a self-amortizing basis with fixed rate terms up to 20 years.&#160;&#160;The
self-amortization loans are generally subject to a $2.0 million maximum loan
amount.&#160;&#160;References to commercial real estate loans below refer to
multi-family and commercial real estate.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The terms
and conditions of each loan are tailored to the needs of the borrower and based
on the financial strength of the project and any guarantors.&#160;&#160;In
reaching a decision on whether to make a commercial real estate loan, we
consider the net operating income of the property, the borrower&#8217;s expertise and
credit history and the value of the underlying property.&#160;&#160;Loan to
value ratios are a very important consideration.&#160;&#160;Generally, however,
commercial real estate loans originated by us will not exceed 80% of the
appraised value or the purchase price of the property, whichever is
less.&#160;&#160;Other factors we consider, with respect to commercial real
estate rental properties, include the term of the lease(s) and the quality of
the tenant(s).&#160;&#160;We generally require that the properties securing
these real estate loans have debt service coverage ratios (the ratio of earnings
before debt service to debt service) of at least 1.2
times.&#160;&#160;Environmental reports are generally required for commercial
real estate loans.&#160;&#160;Commercial real estate loans made to corporations,
partnerships and other business entities may require personal guarantees by the
principals as warranted.&#160;&#160;Property inspections are conducted no less
than every three years, or more frequently as warranted. <font style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;</font>Bank</font>
lending policies allow lending up to the 80% loan to value level and 1.2 times
debt service coverage ratio.&#160;&#160;Over the course of 2009, however, we
have informally reduced our maximum loan to value ratios and increased our
maximum debt service coverage ratio, as well as taking a more conservative
approach on other underwriting issues.&#160;&#160;We believe these actions have
resulted in originations that are more conservative in nature than Bank policy
allows.&#160;&#160;We intend to maintain this conservative posture at least as
long as we perceive a heightened economic risk in this type of
lending.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">A
commercial borrower&#8217;s financial information is monitored on an ongoing basis by
requiring periodic financial statement updates, payment history reviews and
periodic face-to-face meetings with the borrower.&#160;&#160;We require
commercial borrowers to provide annually updated financial statements and
federal tax returns.&#160;&#160;These requirements also apply to the individual
principals of our commercial borrowers.&#160;&#160;We also require borrowers
with rental investment property to provide an annual report of income and
expenses for the property, including a tenant list and copies of leases, as
applicable.&#160;&#160;The largest commercial real estate loan in our portfolio
at June 30, 2009 was a $21.0 million loan located in Ocean County, New Jersey
and secured by a shopping mall.&#160;&#160;This loan was performing according to
its terms at June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;Our largest commercial real estate
relationship consisted of properties located mainly in our primary market area
with a real estate investor.&#160;&#160;The aggregate outstanding loan balance
for this relationship is $40.5 million, and these loans are all performing in
accordance with their terms.</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;

        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">7</font></div>

          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans
secured by commercial real estate, including multi-family properties, generally
involve larger principal amounts and a greater degree of risk than one- to
four-family residential mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;Because payments on loans
secured by commercial real estate are often dependent on successful operation or
management of the properties, repayment of such loans may be affected by adverse
conditions in the real estate market or the economy.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Item 1A,
Risk Factors &#8211; Current Market and Economic Conditions May Significantly Affect
Our Operations and Financial Condition.&#8221;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Second Mortgage
and Equity Loans</font>.&#160;&#160;We also offer second mortgage and equity
loans and home equity of lines of credit, each of which are secured by one- to
four-family residences, substantially all of which are located in our primary
market area.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, second mortgage and equity loans
totaled $54.8 million, or 4.2% of total loans.&#160;&#160;Additionally, at June
30, 2009, the unadvanced amounts of home equity lines of credit totaled $33.8
million.&#160;&#160;The underwriting standards utilized for home equity loans
and equity lines of credit include a determination of the applicant&#8217;s credit
history, an assessment of the applicant&#8217;s ability to meet existing obligations
and payments on the proposed loan and the value of the collateral securing the
loan.&#160;&#160;The combined (first and second mortgage liens) loan-to-value
ratio for home equity loans and equity lines of credit is generally limited to
80%.&#160;&#160;Home equity loans are offered with fixed and adjustable rates of
interest and with terms of up to 30 years.&#160;&#160;Our home equity lines of
credit have adjustable rates of interest which are indexed to the prime rate, as
reported in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">The Wall Street
Journal</font>.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Equity
loans entail greater risk than do residential mortgage loans, particularly if
they are secured by an asset that has a superior security
interest.&#160;&#160;In addition, equity loan collections depend on the
borrower&#8217;s continuing financial stability, and thus are more likely to be
adversely affected by job loss, divorce, illness or personal
bankruptcy.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Construction
Loans.&#160;&#160;</font>We originate construction loans for the development of
one- to four-family residential properties located in our primary market
area.&#160;&#160;Residential construction loans are generally offered to
experienced local developers operating in our primary market area and to
individuals for the construction of their personal residences.&#160;&#160;At
June 30, 2009, residential construction loans amounted to $65.8 million, or 5.1%
of total loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
residential construction loans generally provide for the payment of interest
only during the construction phase, but in no event exceeding 24
months.&#160;&#160;Residential construction loans can be made with a maximum
loan-to-value ratio of 75% of the appraised value of the land and 100% of the
costs associated with the construction.&#160;&#160;Residential construction
loans are generally made on the same terms as our one- to four-family mortgage
loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We also
make construction loans for commercial development projects.&#160;&#160;The
projects include multi-family, apartment, retail and office
buildings.&#160;&#160;We generally require that a commitment for permanent
financing be in place prior to closing the construction loan.&#160;&#160;The
maximum loan-to-value ratio limit applicable to these loans is generally
80%.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, commercial construction loans totaled $65.0
million, or 5.0% of total loans.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, the largest
outstanding commercial construction loan balance was for $15.3 million and is
secured by a condominium project.&#160;&#160;This loan is one of two loans to
the same borrower totaling $18.0 million that are classified as non-accrual and
considered impaired with a specific reserve of $2.8 million at June 30,
2009.&#160;&#160;Oritani charged off $2.0 million of the construction loan as of
June 30, 2009, as this portion has been determined to be an incurred
loss.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Before
making a commitment to fund a construction loan, we require an appraisal on the
property by an independent licensed appraiser.&#160;&#160;We require title
insurance and, if applicable, an environmental survey prior to making a
commitment to fund a construction loan.&#160;&#160;We generally also review and
inspect each property before disbursement of funds during the terms of the
construction loan.&#160;&#160;Loan proceeds are disbursed after inspection based
on the percentage of completion method.</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
      <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">8</font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Construction
and development financing is generally considered to involve a higher degree of
credit risk than long-term financing on improved, owner-occupied real
estate.&#160;&#160;Risk of loss on a construction loan depends largely upon the
accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property at completion of
construction compared to the estimated cost (including interest) of construction
and other assumptions.&#160;&#160;If the estimate of construction cost proves to
be inaccurate, we may be required to advance funds beyond the amount originally
committed in order to protect the value of the
property.&#160;&#160;Additionally, if the estimate of value proves to be
inaccurate, we may be confronted with a project, when completed, having a value
which is insufficient to assure full repayment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We chose
to reduce our exposure to construction lending in 2009 due to current market and
economic conditions.&#160;&#160;Construction originations for the year ended
June 30, 2009 were $45.1 million, versus $99.2 million for the comparable 2008
period.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Other
Loans.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Other
loans primarily consist of business loans and to a smaller extent, account
loans.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>Other Loans
includes $10.7 million of commercial loans to businesses.&#160;&#160;These loans
are unsecured or secured by business assets.&#160;&#160;In 2009, Oritani
curtailed this type of lending.&#160;&#160;Other loans totaled $11.0 million, or
less than 1% of our total loan portfolio at June 30, 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Loan
Originations, Purchases, Sales, Participations and Servicing of
Loans.&#160;&#160;</font>Lending activities are conducted primarily by our loan
personnel operating at our main office.&#160;&#160;All loans originated by us
are underwritten pursuant to our policies and procedures.&#160;&#160;We
originate both adjustable rate and fixed rate loans.&#160;&#160;Our ability to
originate fixed or adjustable rate loans is dependent upon the relative customer
demand for such loans, which is affected by the current and expected future
levels of market interest rates.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We retain
in our portfolio substantially all loans that we originate, although we have
occasionally sold longer-term, fixed-rate one- to four-family residential
mortgage loans into the secondary market.&#160;&#160;There were no sales of
residential mortgage loans in fiscal 2008 or 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Occasionally,
we will also participate in loans, sometimes as the &#8220;lead
lender.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Whether we are the lead lender or not, we underwrite our
participation portion of the loan according to our own underwriting criteria and
procedures.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, we had $68.3 million in loan
participation interests.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At June
30, 2009, we were servicing loans sold in the amount of $15.3
million.&#160;&#160;Loan servicing includes collecting and remitting loan
payments, accounting for principal and interest, contacting delinquent
mortgagors, supervising foreclosures and property dispositions in the event of
unremedied defaults, making certain insurance and tax payments on behalf of the
borrowers and generally administering the loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the fiscal year ended June 30, 2009, we originated $89.9 million of fixed- and
adjustable-rate one- to four-family residential mortgage loans, all of which
were retained by us.&#160;&#160;The fixed-rate loans retained by us consisted
primarily of loans with terms of 30 years or less.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Non-performing
and Problem Assets</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
commence collection efforts when a loan becomes ten days past due with system
generated reminder notices. Subsequent late charges and delinquent notices are
issued and the account is monitored on a regular basis thereafter. Personal,
direct contact with the borrower is attempted early in the collection process as
a courtesy reminder and later to determine the reason for the delinquency and to
safeguard our collateral. When a loan is more than 45 days past due, the credit
file is reviewed and, if deemed necessary, information is updated or confirmed
and collateral re-evaluated.&#160;&#160;We make every effort to contact the
borrower and develop a plan of repayment to cure the delinquency.&#160;&#160;A
summary report of all loans 30 days or more past due is reported to the Board of
Directors.&#160;&#160;If no repayment plan is in process and the loan is
delinquent at least two payments, the file is referred to counsel for the
commencement of foreclosure or other collection efforts.</font></div><br>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>

      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loans are
placed on non-accrual status when they are more than 90 days
delinquent.&#160;&#160;When loans are placed on a non-accrual status, unpaid
accrued interest is fully reversed.&#160;&#160;Once the outstanding principal
balance is brought current, income is recognized to the extent it is deemed
collectible.&#160;&#160;If the deficiencies causing the delinquency are
resolved, such loans may be placed on accrual status once all arrearages are
resolved.&#160;&#160;See additional discussion regarding our non-performing
assets at June 30, 2009 in &#8220;Management Discussion and Analysis.&#8221;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Non-Performing
Assets</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">.&#160;&#160;</font>The table below
sets forth the amounts and categories of our non-performing assets at the dates
indicated.&#160;&#160;At each date presented, we had no troubled debt
restructurings (loans for which a portion of interest or principal has been
forgiven and loans modified at interest rates materially less than current
market rates).</font></div>

      mortgage loan balances:</font></div>
                </td>
                <td valign="bottom" width="1%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition to the delinquent loans listed above, we had loans that were delinquent
90 days or more past due as to principal.&#160;&#160;Such loans had passed their
maturity date but continued making monthly payments, keeping their interest
current.&#160;&#160;All such loans have subsequently been paid in full or were
extended by us, which negated their past due maturity status.&#160;&#160;These
loans totaled $3.1 million, $316,000, and $3.2 million at June 30, 2009, 2008
and 2007, respectively.</font></div><br>

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Real Estate
Owned</font>.&#160;&#160;Real estate acquired by us as a result of foreclosure
or by deed in lieu of foreclosure is classified as real estate owned until
sold.&#160;&#160;When property is acquired it is recorded at the lower of cost
or fair market value at the date of foreclosure, establishing a new cost
basis.&#160;&#160;Holding costs and declines in fair value result in charges to
expense after acquisition.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009 and 2008, we had no real
estate owned.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to June 30, 2009, Oritani obtained title to
the property securing the $877,000 non-performing loan classified as
impaired.&#160;&#160;The property is currently being marketed for
sale.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial
Condition and Results of Operations- Comparison of Operating Results for the
Years Ended June 30, 2009 and June 30, 2008, Provision for Loan
Losses.&#8221;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Classified
Assets.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">&#160;</font>Federal regulations
provide that loans and other assets of lesser quality should be classified as
&#8220;substandard,&#8221; &#8220;doubtful&#8221; or &#8220;loss&#8221; assets.&#160;&#160;An asset is considered
&#8220;substandard&#8221; if it is inadequately protected by the current net worth and
paying capacity of the obligor or of the collateral pledged, if
any.&#160;&#160;&#8220;Substandard&#8221; assets include those characterized by the
&#8220;distinct possibility&#8221; that we will sustain &#8220;some loss&#8221; if the deficiencies are
not corrected.&#160;&#160;Assets classified as &#8220;doubtful&#8221; have all of the
weaknesses inherent in those classified &#8220;substandard,&#8221; with the added
characteristic that the weaknesses present make &#8220;collection or liquidation in
full,&#8221; on the basis of currently existing facts, conditions, and values, &#8220;highly
questionable and improbable.&#8221;&#160;&#160;Assets classified as &#8220;loss&#8221; are those
considered &#8220;uncollectible&#8221; and of such little value that their continuance as
assets without the establishment of a specific loss reserve is not
warranted.&#160;&#160;We classify an asset as &#8220;special mention&#8221; if the asset has
a potential weakness that warrants management&#8217;s close
attention.&#160;&#160;While such assets are not impaired, management has
concluded that if the potential weakness in the asset is not addressed, the
value of the asset may deteriorate, adversely affecting the repayment of the
asset.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We are
required to establish general allowances for loan losses for loans classified
substandard or doubtful, as well as for other problem loans.&#160;&#160;General
allowances represent loss allowances which have been established to recognize
the inherent losses associated with lending activities, but which, unlike
specific allowances, have not been allocated to particular problem
assets.&#160;&#160;When we classify problem assets as &#8220;loss,&#8221; we are required
either to establish a specific allowance for losses equal to 100% of the amount
of the asset so classified or to charge off such amount.&#160;&#160;Our
determination as to the classification of our assets and the amount of our
valuation allowances is subject to review by the Federal Deposit Insurance
Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) and the New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance
(&#8220;the Department&#8221;) which can order the establishment of additional general or
specific loss allowances.&#160;&#160;Such examinations typically occur
annually.&#160;&#160;Our last examination was as of March 31, 2009 by the
FDIC.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
following table shows the aggregate amounts of our classified assets at the date
indicated for both residential real estate and non-residential real estate
loans.&#160;&#160;The amount of assets classified as &#8220;substandard&#8221; in the table
includes nine commercial real estate loans at June 30, 2009, three residential
and four commercial real estate loans at June 30, 2008 and two commercial real
estate loans at June 30, 2007.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The loan
portfolio is reviewed on a regular basis to determine whether any loans require
classification in accordance with applicable regulations.&#160;&#160;Not all
classified assets constitute non-performing assets.&#160;&#160;The increases in
Special Mention and Substandard assets is primarily due to increased delinquent,
nonaccrual and impaired loans.&#160;&#160;See &#8220;Item 7. Management&#8217;s Discussion
and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations- Comparison of
Operating Results for the Years Ended June 30, 2009 and June 30, 2008, Provision
for Loan Losses.&#8221;</font></div><br>

      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 8pt; COLOR: #000000; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;
</font></div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Impaired
Loans</font>.&#160;&#160;The Company defines an impaired loan as a loan for
which it is probable, based on current information, that the Company will not
collect all amounts due under the contractual terms of the loan
agreement.&#160;&#160;Loans we individually classify as impaired include
multifamily, commercial mortgage and construction loans.&#160;&#160;Impaired
loans are individually assessed to determine that each loan&#8217;s carrying value is
not in excess of the fair value of the related collateral or the present value
of the expected future cash flows.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">If the
loan&#8217;s carrying value does exceed the fair value, specific reserves are
established to reduce the loan&#8217;s carrying value. For classification purposes,
impaired loans are typically classified as substandard. </font>Residential
mortgage and consumer loans are deemed smaller balance homogeneous loans which
are evaluated collectively for impairment and are therefore excluded from the
population of impaired loans.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Potential Problem
Loans</font>.&#160;&#160;Although we believe that substantially all risk
elements at June 30, 2009 have been disclosed in the categories presented above,
it is possible that for a variety of reasons, including economic conditions,
certain borrowers may be unable to comply with the contractual repayment terms
on certain real estate and commercial loans. As part of the analysis of the loan
portfolio, management determined that there were approximately $14.0 million in
potential problem loans at June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;There is one large loan in
the 60-89 day past due total at June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Subsequent
to June 30, 2009, the delinquency of this loan exceeded 90 days and it was
placed on non-accrual status. </font>This is a $14.0 million loan secured by a
commercial property in Hudson County, New Jersey.&#160;&#160;The borrower has
experienced cash flow difficulties.&#160;&#160;Foreclosure proceedings have
commenced&#160;although Oritani is in negotiations with the borrower regarding
potential resolution.&#160;&#160;It is presently unknown whether&#160;these
negotiations will be successful, or whether continued pursuit of legal remedies
will be necessary.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allowance
for Loan Losses</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
allowance for loan losses is maintained at a level necessary to absorb loan
losses that are both probable and reasonably estimable.&#160;&#160;Management,
in determining the allowance for loan losses, considers the losses inherent in
our loan portfolio and changes in the nature and volume of loan activities,
along with the general economic and real estate market conditions.&#160;&#160;A
description of our methodology in establishing our allowance for loan losses is
set forth in the section &#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial
Condition and Results of Operations - Critical Accounting Policies-Allowance for
Loan Losses.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The allowance for loan losses as of June 30, 2009 was
maintained at a level that represents management&#8217;s best estimate of losses
inherent in the loan portfolio, and such losses were both probable and
reasonably estimable. However, this analysis process is inherently subjective,
as it requires us to make estimates that are susceptible to revisions as more
information becomes available.&#160;&#160;Although we believe that we have
established the allowance at levels to absorb probable and estimable losses,
future additions may be necessary if economic or other conditions in the future
differ from the current environment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition, as an integral part of their examination process, the FDIC, OTS, and
the Department has authority to periodically review our allowance for loan
losses.&#160;&#160;Such agencies may require that we recognize additions to the
allowance based on their judgments of information available to them at the time
of their examination.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
increase in the allowance for loan losses, and related provision, is primarily
due to the large increases in delinquent and impaired loans at June 30, 2009,
versus June 30, 2008.&#160;&#160;Such loans are discussed in Item 7,
&#8220;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of
Operations.&#8221;&#160;&#160;In addition, the continued increase in the multi-family
and commercial real estate loan portfolio was also a factor.&#160;&#160;These
types of loans inherently contain more credit risk than one- to four family
residential loans.&#160;&#160;Although we had some experience in this type of
lending prior to this significant growth, the increased volume of such
originations during the last&#160;six years heightens the credit risk associated
with this portion of the loan portfolio.&#160;&#160;Therefore, in order to
adequately establish the allowance at levels sufficient to absorb probable and
estimable losses in the loan portfolio, we focus on the ratio of the allowance
to total loans as well as other measurement factors.&#160;&#160;This analysis
incorporates our review of various sources of industry data relating to the
allowance for loan losses, including peer group reviews.&#160;&#160;Due to the
continued focus on this type of lending, we have increased the allowance for
loan losses, and related provision, during periods of significant multi-family
and commercial loan growth.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Investments</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The Board
of Directors is responsible for adopting our investment policy.&#160;&#160;The
investment policy is reviewed periodically by management and any changes to the
policy are recommended to and subject to the approval of the Board of
Directors.&#160;&#160;Authority to make investments under the approved
investment policy guidelines is delegated<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>to appropriate
officers.&#160;&#160;While general investment strategies are developed and
authorized by the Board of Directors, the execution of specific actions
primarily rests with Oritani Bank&#8217;s President, Chief Financial Officer and
Asset/Liability Committee, which have responsibility for ensuring that the
guidelines and requirements included in the investment policy are followed and
that all securities are considered prudent for investment.&#160;&#160;Each of
our Chief Financial Officer, President and Asset/Liability Committee have
increasing authority to purchase various types of investments; all individual
investment purchases in excess of $20.0 million and all daily purchases in
excess of $30 million must be approved by our Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;All
investment transactions are reviewed and ratified or approved (as the case may
be) at regularly scheduled meetings of the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;Any
investment which, subsequent to its purchase, fails to meet the guidelines of
the policy is reported to the Board of Directors at its next meeting where the
Board decides whether to hold or sell the investment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">New
Jersey-chartered savings banks have authority to invest in various types of
assets, including U.S. Treasury obligations, securities of various federal
agencies, mortgage-backed securities, certain certificates of deposit of insured
financial institutions, overnight and short-term loans to other banks, corporate
debt instruments, and Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac equity
securities.&#160;&#160;Oritani Financial Corp., as a federally chartered
mid-tier stock holding company, may invest in equity securities subject to
certain limitations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
investment policy requires that all securities transactions be conducted in a
safe and sound manner.&#160;&#160;Investment decisions must be based upon a
thorough analysis of each security instrument to determine if its quality and
inherent risks fit within Oritani Bank&#8217;s overall asset/liability management
objectives, the effect on its risk-based capital measurement and the prospects
for yield and/or appreciation.&#160;&#160;The investment policy provides that
Oritani Bank may invest in U.S. treasury notes, U.S. and state agency
securities, mortgage-backed securities, and other conservative investment
opportunities.&#160;&#160;Typical investments are currently in U.S. agency
securities and government sponsored mortgage-backed securities.</font></div><br>

    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
investment portfolio at June 30, 2009, consisted of $134.9 million in federal
agency obligations, a $5.7 million investment in a mutual fund, $2.2 million of
corporate debt instruments and $1.8 million in equity securities.&#160;&#160;We
also invest in mortgage-backed securities, most of which are guaranteed by
government sponsored enterprises.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our
mortgage-backed securities portfolio totaled $247.4 million, or 12.9% of total
assets, and consisted of $191.4 million in fixed-rate securities and $56.0
million in adjustable-rate securities, primarily guaranteed by Fannie Mae,
Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160;Securities can be classified as held to
maturity or available for sale at the date of purchase.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">U.S. Government
and Federal Agency Obligations.</font>&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our
U.S.&#160;Government and federal agency securities portfolio totaled $134.9
million, all of which was classified as available for sale.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Corporate
Bonds</font>.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our corporate bond portfolio totaled
$2.2 million, which consisted of one security, rated BBB- and was classified as
available for sale.&#160;&#160;The industry represented by our corporate bond
issuer was financial.&#160;&#160;Although corporate bonds may offer higher
yields than U.S. Treasury or agency securities of comparable duration, corporate
bonds also have a higher risk of default due to possible adverse changes in the
credit-worthiness of the issuer.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Mutual
Funds.</font>&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our mutual fund portfolio totaled
$5.7 million, or 0.3% of our total assets, all of which were classified as
available for sale.&#160;&#160;The portfolio consisted of an investment in a
mutual fund that holds adjustable-rate mortgage loans and similar
securities.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2009, the portfolio was deemed
other-than-temporarily impaired and the Company recorded a non-cash impairment
charge to earnings of $1.7 million for the year ended June 30,
2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Equity
Securities.</font>&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009, our equity securities portfolio
totaled $1.8 million, or 0.1% of our total assets, all of which were classified
as available for sale.&#160;&#160;The portfolio consists of financial industry
common stock.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2009, several of these holdings were
deemed other-than-temporarily impaired and the Company recorded a non-cash
impairment charge to earnings of $399,000.&#160;&#160;Equity securities are not
insured or guaranteed investments and are affected by market interest rates and
stock market fluctuations.&#160;&#160;Such investments are carried at their fair
value and fluctuations in the fair value of such investments, including
temporary declines in value, directly affect out net capital
position.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-STYLE: italic">Mortgage-Backed
Securities.&#160;&#160;</font>We purchase mortgage-backed securities primarily
insured or guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160;We
invest in mortgage-backed securities to achieve positive interest rate spreads
with minimal administrative expense, and to lower our credit risk as a result of
the guarantees provided by Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae or Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160;Our
investment policy also authorizes the investment in collateralized mortgage
obligations (&#8220;CMOs&#8221;), also insured or issued by Freddie Mac, Fannie Mae and
Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160;&#160;We limit CMO investments to those classes of CMOs
carrying the most stable cash flows and lowest prepayment risk of any class of
CMOs and which pass the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council&#8217;s
average life restriction tests at the time of purchase.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Mortgage-backed
securities are created by the pooling of mortgages and the issuance of a
security with an interest rate which is less than the interest rate on the
underlying mortgages.&#160;&#160;Mortgage-backed securities typically represent
a participation interest in a pool of single-family or multi-family mortgages,
although we focus our investments on mortgage-backed securities backed by one-
to four-family mortgages.&#160;&#160;The issuers of such securities (generally
U.S.&#160;government agencies and government sponsored enterprises, including
Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae) pool and resell the participation
interests in the form of securities to investors such as us, and guarantee the
payment of principal and interest to investors.&#160;&#160;Mortgage-backed
securities generally yield less than the loans that underlie such securities
because of the cost of payment guarantees and credit
enhancements.&#160;&#160;However, mortgage-backed securities are usually more
liquid than individual mortgage loans and may be used to collateralize our
specific liabilities and obligations.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At June
30, 2009, our mortgage-backed securities totaled $247.4 million or 12.9%, of
total assets and 13.6% of interest earning assets.&#160;&#160;At June 30, 2009,
22.6% of the mortgage-backed securities were backed by adjustable rate mortgage
loans and 77.4% were backed by fixed rate mortgage loans.&#160;&#160;The
mortgage-backed securities portfolio had a weighted average yield of 4.43% at
June 30, 2009.&#160;&#160;The estimated fair value of our mortgage-backed
securities at June 30, 2009 was $249.0 million, which is $5.1 million more than
the amortized cost of $243.9 million.&#160;&#160;Investments in mortgage-backed
securities involve a risk that actual prepayments may differ from estimated
prepayments over the life of the security, which may require adjustments to the
amortization of any premium or accretion of any discount relating to such
instruments thereby changing the net yield on such securities.&#160;&#160;There
is also reinvestment risk associated with the cash flows from such securities or
if such securities are redeemed by the issuer.&#160;&#160;In addition, the
market value of such securities may be adversely affected by changes in interest
rates.&#160;&#160;All of the Company&#8217;s mortgage-backed securities are insured or
guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae except for one AAA rated
private label CMO with an amortized cost of $1.0 million and a fair value of
$860,000.&#160;&#160;The security was issued in 2003 and is performing in
accordance with contractual terms.</font></div>
